body:
@azzazzel the WARN log is new to 1.0.0.CR1 (new version of Agroal) but the root cause is that the `stream()` method needs a transaction.

If you manage the transaction by yourself, maybe there is something wrong at this level, cannot say anything without the full source code but if it's on a separate thread you may need some sort of context propagation.

If possible, the best is to do transaction management the Quarkus way: https://quarkus.io/guides/transaction

Else, you can look at context propagation but I'm not sure it's the issue here: https://quarkus.io/guides/context-propagation

@sirf is right, steams that perform I/O operations should be closed in order to properly release resources. It's on the Stream JavaDoc: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/stream/Stream.html

> Streams have a BaseStream.close() method and implement AutoCloseable, but nearly all stream instances do not actually need to be closed after use. Generally, only streams whose source is an IO channel (such as those returned by Files.lines(Path, Charset)) will require closing.

In Hibernate with Panache, `stream()` performs I/O operations so it should be closed manually via `close()` or via a try-with-resource construct to properly close the underlying ResultSet/Statement. If you don't do this, Agroal will log a warning and close the Resultset/Statement for you, that's why it didn't crash :)

Maybe we can add to the documentation guide a more complete example about using the `stream()` methods.

"You live, you learn" ;)

Thanks for the explanation! Indeed explicitly closing the stream, does not result in warning. 
Perhaps this should be added (and even highlighted) in the documentation. AFACT explicitly closing streams is not widely popular practice. 

Also, (asking out of curiosity) is there any reason not to close the Resultset/Statement on terminal operations on the stream?

> Also, (asking out of curiosity) is there any reason not to close the Resultset/Statement on terminal operations on the stream?

I suspect this should be done by the JDBC driver ... so we cannot do anything about it.

I'll try to update the guide with some insight

Thank you all for your help!

I'm not sure if you want to keep this issue open until the docs are updated so I'm not closing it yet. Please close it whenever you find it appropriate.
